findings.claim: R21 is not closed: README, the repair commit message, and ADR-017 publish a property `published-band-matches-the-ledger` does not enforce, and the shipped band violates that published property — the ADR names 66.23s as "Slowest recorded `fast` run at 122 cases" while the ledger committed in the same tree records 14 runs at 122 cases topping out at 66.48s, and the derivation sentence still multiplies a run (65.53s) that exists only in the superseded 119-case ledger.
findings.evidence: README.md:98-102 — "the committed ceiling must be at least the rule applied to the ledger's slowest run at the current case count, AND the published maximum must be at least that run"; commit 3699b87's message repeats it verbatim. The grader implements no such thing: src/browser/eval_adapter.py:417-421 is `if rule(said) != rule(slowest)` — band equality, so `published` may sit up to ~1.0s below the ledger max at these magnitudes and still pass. It currently does: ADR-017:58 publishes `66.23s — 8 runs`, and `git show HEAD:evals/report/history.jsonl` has 14 rows with suite=fast/total=122, max 66.48 (6 of the published-as-complete run list absent, the two slowest omitted — the same shape R21 named). ADR-017:62 then says "gives 65.53 x 1.15 = 75.4 -> 80" — 65.53 is not a 122-case run at all (it is from the 119-case ledger), i.e. "a ceiling derived from a maximum that was never measured" reappears in the paragraph that condemns it; fast-wall-clock-budget provenance (10) carries the same 65.53 under "re-derived from every run the ledger records at the shipped case count". NON-BLOCKING HALF, stated plainly by the reviewer: the ceiling itself is right — rule(66.48) = 80 = WALL_BUDGET_S['fast'], so nothing is under-gated; what ships false is the claim about what is checked and which run was slowest.
findings.repro: `_check_published_band()` -> {'passed': True}; `git show HEAD:evals/report/history.jsonl` filtered to suite=fast/total=122 -> 14 runs, max 66.48, against ADR-017:58's '66.23s — 8 runs'. `grep -c '65.53' specs/decisions/ADR-017-*.md` -> 1, and `"wall_s": 65.53` appears only on 119-case rows.
findings.acceptance: Either the grader enforces the property README states (`published >= ledger max`, run list regenerated by script at commit time), or README:98-102, ADR-017 §2 and the commit-message wording describe the property actually enforced (same-band derivation) and label the run list as a snapshot at a named sha rather than 'every run the ledger records'; ADR-017's derivation line multiplies the ledger max at the shipped case count (66.48 x 1.15 = 76.5 -> 80), and fast-wall-clock-budget provenance (10) is corrected the same way. Watched red first by putting a published value one band low.

findings.claim: The R20 fix introduces a new false refusal it does not declare: a plural aggregate request whose plan correctly declares `rank: false` is now killed as `failure:task`, and the refusal text tells the planner to declare `rank: true` — which would return one product for a question that asked for several.
findings.evidence: src/browser/agent.py:200-221 refuses whenever `is_aggregate(task)` and the single `extract_all` does not carry `rank is True`. `_AGGREGATE` (verifier.py:187-190) is `\b(which|what|who)\b.{0,80}\b(most|least|fewest|highest|lowest|greatest)\b` — it matches "Which products in this catalogue have the lowest prices?", which is not a which-ONE-of-a-set question. End-to-end on shop.html with the same plan as plan-lint-refuses-a-declared-non-comparison: status failure:task, answer null, budgets.actions 1, reason "...Declare `rank: true` and let code do the comparison...". At 117301e the same input returned the four-row list as success, so this is a regression introduced by the round-4 repair. Nothing declares it: no case, and grep for 'plural' across ADR-016-m31, specs/001, docs/support-matrix.md and tasks/TODO.md returns nothing. ADR-016's justification for the fix ("`_AGGREGATE` is narrow and high-precision: when it matches, code is entitled to contradict a `rank: false`") is falsified by that one input. NOTE: this fails LOUD — it is a false refusal, not a wrong answer published as success.
findings.repro: run_case on plan-lint-refuses-a-declared-non-comparison with task 'Which products in this catalogue have the lowest prices?' -> failure:task, answer null
findings.acceptance: Either the lint's precondition is narrowed so a plural which-question is not treated as which-one (no new wording regex needed — the existing match already exposes the number), or ADR-016's 'entitled to contradict' paragraph and a debt block state this ceiling with this exact input as its evidence, and a case pins the behaviour so it is a decision rather than a side effect.

findings.claim: The merge weakens M34's R2-1 offset anchoring for every enumerated row but the first, and docs/support-matrix.md D24 still claims the window is anchored to the DOM occurrence for all extractions; no eval case exercises `extract_all` through the `not_page_furniture` path at all.
findings.evidence: src/browser/agent.py:675-676 — `off = (real_offset if v == vals[0] else _closest_occurrence(body, v, -1))`; rows 2..n of an `extract_all` get hint -1, i.e. plain first-occurrence, which is exactly the pre-R2-1 behaviour PR #30 R2-1 fixed. docs/support-matrix.md:67 (D24) says the context is "anchored to the actual DOM occurrence it was read from" and lists three uncaught shapes; this fourth one is not among them (it is only in a source comment). `loc.first` itself is the right call — `loc.evaluate` on a multi-match locator is a strict-mode violation — and the row-wise judging claim does hold (verify() with two extraction records fails the set when only the second row's context repeats on the other page, checked directly). But every M34 case uses `extract`, so the merged `extract_all` x `other_page_text` path is asserted in the resolution artifact and graded nowhere.
findings.repro: `grep -n 'off = (real_offset' src/browser/agent.py`; `grep -l 'extract_all' evals/adversarial/*.json | xargs grep -l 'other_page_text'` -> no matches
findings.acceptance: D24 names the residual ("for `extract_all`, only the first value gets a DOM-derived offset; later rows fall back to first-occurrence"), or the hint is taken per-row via `loc.nth(i)`; plus one adversarial case running an `extract_all` across two pages where one enumerated row is chrome, watched red against a build that judges the set by row 0's evidence.
